judgment.rationale: Both SFIs are Grade R, Term 3 Skill bullets printed in the same 'Emergent reading skills' sub-strand row under the EMERGENT READING skill area (identical ancestry: Grade R > Term 3 > Emergent Reading > Emergent reading skills; same source page 49). Substantively they are coherent but distinct emergent-reading behaviours concerning the picture/print relationship: 'Uses pictures to understand simple phrases and sentences in a book' is picture-supported meaning-making from text, while 'Distinguishes pictures from print: points to a word and asks what the word is' is print awareness (recognising that words, not pictures, carry the printed message). The LC tags overlap meaningfully ('emergent reading', 'pictures'), supporting genuine conceptual coherence. However, neither statement shows expanded capability over the other: same grade, same term, same sub-strand, no increase in text length, letter range, or independence, and CAPS presents them as parallel co-taught bullets rather than as a sequence. The evidence does not justify asserting that proficiency in either materially supports success in the other, so a symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment rather than a directional buildsTowards. Note that both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each) and all nodes carry upstream audit/merge context; the bounded excerpts shown are nonetheless clear, unambiguous printed bullet text, so the limitation does not make the judgment ambiguous.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade R Emergent Reading Skills under the sub-strand 'Relates sounds to letters and words', with LC tags sharing 'phonological awareness', 'sounds', 'words'. The first (Grade R, Term 1 per identity scope) is the initial insight that words are made up of sounds, evidenced only by isolating the beginning sound of one's own name; the second (Grade R, Term 2) extends this to understanding that a word consists of several sounds and segmenting a whole word aurally (sat - s-a-t). This is substantive expansion from a single initial-sound judgement on a familiar word to full aural segmentation, and the Term 1 capability supports success at the Term 2 capability, so direction runs from the earlier Term 1 skill to the later Term 2 skill within the same grade. judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit under Grade 2 (rank 2) > Reading and Phonics > Phonics ('Daily Phonic Activities of 15 minutes'), but in different terms: the second SFI is Grade 2 Term 3 ('Builds words using the consonant and vowel digraphs, consonant blends and double consonants taught this year') and the first is Grade 2 Term 4 ('Recognises at least 5 new vowel digraphs ... ar, er, ir, or, ur'). Within one Grade, a developmental direction may only run from the earlier Term to the later Term, so only second_to_first is available. Semantically that direction is supportable: secure grapheme-level knowledge and active word-building with the digraphs, blends and double consonants already taught in Term 3 (LC tags 'digraphs', 'phonics', 'blends', 'word building') gives learners the digraph concept and decoding/encoding routine needed to take on an additional set of five new r-controlled vowel digraphs in Term 4 (LC tags 'phonics', 'vowel digraphs', 'recognises'), an extension of the same phonics content to new grapheme patterns rather than mere repeated wording. Confidence is moderate because the more intuitive recognition-then-building order would run Term 4 to Term 3, which the within-grade ordering rule disallows, and both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each); endpoints and ancestors also carry upstream audit/merge context, including merged Grade 2 and Term banner nodes.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade R, Term 2, Emergent Reading (same coordinate rank 0), but under different Sub-strands: 'Phonological/Phonemic Awareness' (identifies rhyming words in well known rhymes and songs, e.g. Humpty Dumpty) and 'Relates sounds to letters and words' (understands that words consist of more than one sound, e.g. sat - s-a-t done aurally). The shared LC tag 'phonological awareness' plus the aural focus of both statements shows genuine skill coherence rather than mere wording overlap. Both endpoints carry truncated source and LC evidence, so a stronger dependency claim is not warranted on this bounded record.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs sit in Grade R (rank 0) Emergent Reading. The first is Term 1, sub-strand 'Begins to make meaning of written text': 'Understands that print communicates meaning: a word can represent one's own name'. The second is Term 4, sub-strand 'Phonological/Phonemic Awareness': 'Recognises and names some letters of the alphabet such as letters in own name' (LCs: recognises / names letters of the alphabet). The shared concrete anchor is the learner's own name, but the demand changes substantively: from whole-word print-awareness (a printed word stands for my name) to finer-grained letter-level identification and naming of alphabet letters within that name. Knowing that print carries meaning and attending to one's own written name plausibly supports the later letter recognition/naming work, so the earlier Term 1 statement builds towards the Term 4 statement (permitted earlier-to-later direction within Grade R). This is inferred curriculum coherence, not asserted prerequisite necessity; both endpoints' source evidence is truncated and carries upstream merge/audit context, which limits confirmation beyond the bounded excerpts.

judgment.rationale: First SFI (Grade R, rank 0, Term 1, Emergent Writing) is 'Contributes ideas for a class news book by means of drawings'; second SFI (Grade 1, rank 1, Term 4, Writing / 'Shared, Group and Independent Writing') is 'Organises information into a simple graphic form such as chart or timeline, e.g. uses a chart to record the results of a survey on how children come to school'. Both sit in the shared/group writing line and both have learners record and communicate meaning through non-prose graphic means within a class product, which is substantive, pair-specific instructional coherence rather than generic repetition or mere hierarchy/word overlap. However, the capabilities differ in kind: the Grade R item is about generating and contributing ideas pictorially for a teacher-scribed class text, while the Grade 1 item is about selecting and structuring information into a conventional organiser (chart, timeline). Proficiency in drawing contributions does not specifically support success in graphic information organisation on this evidence, so the permitted forward buildsTowards is not semantically supported despite the lower-to-higher grade ranks; canonical symmetric relatesTo is the correct complete judgment and direction is null. Evidence limits: both endpoints omit 24 source-evidence items and all endpoint/ancestor nodes carry upstream audit/merge context (merged Grade R, Term 1, Grade 1 and Term 4 banner nodes), so the judgment rests on statement text, resolved Grade coordinates and LC tags ('drawings','emergent writing' vs 'chart','organising information','timeline','writing'); nomination signals were weak (jaccard 0.10 on tag 'writing'; shared tokens 'a','of'; weak local_rank_proximity).

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade R, Term 3, Skill Area EMERGENT READING (rank 0, same term), but under different sub-strands: 'Independent Reading' ('Reads' books independently for pleasure, turning pages correctly, showing respect for books; LCs on independent reading, book handling, respect for books) and 'Shared Reading' (uses the cover and illustrations to predict the storyline; LC tagged book cover, illustrations, prediction). They are complementary emergent-reading behaviours around books — positive engagement/print-handling alongside meaning-making prediction from visual cues — with no evidence that proficiency in one is developmentally required for or materially increases likelihood of success in the other, and same-term placement supplies no directional evidence. The overlap evidence is weak (single shared token/tag 'book', adjacent source pages), so a symmetric conceptual coherence judgment is appropriate rather than buildsTowards. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated and the first endpoint's LC evidence is truncated, limiting fuller comparison.
